name: Haplorchis taichui

taxonomy.rank_note: Reference groups can include multiple species. Protozoan higher-rank systems differ; the lineage is provided without forcing every clade into a class rank.

morphology: Egg: roughly 27–32 × 13–18 µm in published descriptions, with host-dependent variation; small, brownish, embryonated and operculated.
Adults are tiny intestinal flukes; fine adult anatomy is more informative than routine egg appearance.

transmission.detail: Snail development is followed by metacercarial encystment in freshwater fish; ingestion leads to intestinal adults and stool eggs.

life_cycle.detail: Snail development is followed by metacercarial encystment in freshwater fish; ingestion leads to intestinal adults and stool eggs.
Eggs in stool; recovered adults or molecular material for species confirmation.

hosts: Definitive: humans and other fish-eating mammals. Intermediate: snail and freshwater fish.
distribution: Thailand and neighboring Mekong countries; distribution depends on fish consumption and local host ecology.
clinical_significance: Can cause intestinal irritation, abdominal discomfort and diarrhea; coinfection with other fish-borne flukes complicates attribution.
specimen: Eggs in stool; recovered adults or molecular material for species confirmation.
diagnostics: Wet mount/concentration at about 400× identifies small-fluke eggs.
Use validated molecular or adult identification for species-level research labels.
differential_diagnosis: Routine eggs can resemble OV and other MIF species; shell appearance alone is not a dependable species label.
review_status: Source-compiled educational content; not independently clinically validated

annotation_guidance: Record specimen, stage, stain, objective/total magnification, pixel calibration, source image and reviewer certainty.
Native crops of 200–650 pixels do not determine biological size. Retain µm-per-pixel calibration before resizing.
Split training, validation and test data by patient/specimen; keep related crops in the same split.
Keep damaged or ambiguous objects uncertain. Molecular confirmation of a mixed specimen does not assign every pictured object a species.
